g.text: Spatial embodied intelligence relies on active
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Spatial embodied intelligence relies on active exploration.

g.text: embodied agents act to acquire observations
Unlike disembodied systems that passively process fixed
observations, an embodied agent could take actions to alter its
position in the environment as exploration, selectively acquiring
observations needed to construct spatial knowledge…
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) Unlike disembodied systems that passively process fixed observations, an embodied agent could take actions to alter its position in the environment as exploration, selectively acquiring observations needed to construct spatial knowledge for various spatial tasks.

g.text: Cognitive science shows that such active exploration leads to
substantially better spatial understanding than passively
receiving the same information, even when observations are
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) Cognitive science shows that such active exploration leads to substantially better spatial understanding than passively receiving the same information, even when observations are identical (Held & Hein, 1963; Chrastil & Warren, 2012; 2013).

g.text: But exploration isn't simply about collecting more
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) But exploration isn't simply about collecting more observations.

g.text: It is about efficiency, acting under uncertainty to target what is
unknown or ambiguous in the agent's spatial belief and maximize
g.title: N4b [Context] (cites=0) It is about efficiency, acting under uncertainty to target what is unknown or ambiguous in the agent's spatial belief and maximize information gain.

g.text: We propose THEORY OF SPACE as a framework
that explicitly treats exploration as a
decoupled from any single downstream task…
g.title: N5 [Method] (cites=0) We propose THEORY OF SPACE as a framework that explicitly treats exploration as a first-class decision-making problem, decoupled from any single downstream task, focusing on opening the box of the agent's internal spatial belief.

g.text: Just as Theory of Mind (ToM) measures how agents model
the hidden mental states of others, THEORY OF SPACE
assesses an agent's ability to model the hidden
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=0) Just as Theory of Mind (ToM) measures how agents model the hidden mental states of others, THEORY OF SPACE assesses an agent's ability to model the hidden physical structure of the world.

g.text: We define THEORY OF SPACE as an embodied
revise in a dynamic environment, and
exploit an internal spatial belief formed…
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) We define THEORY OF SPACE as an embodied agent's ability to actively construct, revise in a dynamic environment, and exploit an internal spatial belief formed through active exploration.

g.text: Beyond end-task evaluation, THEORY OF SPACE directly probes what
the agent knows, what remains uncertain, and how effectively its
actions reduce those uncertainties, measured by the number of
exploration steps and the uncertainty resolved…
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) Beyond end-task evaluation, THEORY OF SPACE directly probes what the agent knows, what remains uncertain, and how effectively its actions reduce those uncertainties, measured by the number of exploration steps and the uncertainty resolved per action.

g.text: Figure 1 provides an overview of THEORY OF SPACE's active
exploration, belief probing, and end-task evaluation.
g.title: P8 [Proof] (cites=0) Figure 1 provides an overview of THEORY OF SPACE's active exploration, belief probing, and end-task evaluation.

g.text: We apply THEORY OF SPACE to evaluate multimodal language models,
which are promising candidates for embodied agents.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) We apply THEORY OF SPACE to evaluate multimodal language models, which are promising candidates for embodied agents.

g.text: By integrating vision and language, they support unified perception,
reasoning, and action over time, yet existing foundation-model benchmarks
offer little insight into these capabilities.
g.title: N10 [Limitation] (cites=0) By integrating vision and language, they support unified perception, reasoning, and action over time, yet existing foundation-model benchmarks offer little insight into these capabilities.

g.text: Most current benchmarks fall into two categories:
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Most current benchmarks fall into two categories:

g.text: passive (Weston et al., 2015; Shi et al., 2022; Yang et al.,
2025c; Gholami et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025a), where the agent
is only asked to reason over given observations,
g.title: N11a [Prior_Work: passive] (cites=5) passive (Weston et al., 2015; Shi et al., 2022; Yang et al., 2025c; Gholami et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025a), where the agent is only asked to reason over given observations,

g.text: and task-driven (Gordon et al., 2018; Shridhar et al., 2020b; Li
et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025b), where the agent must achieve a
g.title: N11b [Prior_Work: task-driven] (cites=4) and task-driven (Gordon et al., 2018; Shridhar et al., 2020b; Li et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2025b), where the agent must achieve a specific goal (e.g., "find the red chair").

g.text: In this work, we propose to systematically
evaluate the active process of spatial
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=0) In this work, we propose to systematically evaluate the active process of spatial belief construction.

g.text: Unlike passive benchmarks, our THEORY OF SPACE benchmark requires
agents to actively explore via moving, rotating, and observing to
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=0) Unlike passive benchmarks, our THEORY OF SPACE benchmark requires agents to actively explore via moving, rotating, and observing to build coherent global beliefs.

g.text: We implement a scalable environment using ThreeDWorld (Gan et al.,
2021) and Objaverse (Deitke et al., 2022) that provides Text-based
and Vision-based worlds to localize perception versus reasoning
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=2) We implement a scalable environment using ThreeDWorld (Gan et al., 2021) and Objaverse (Deitke et al., 2022) that provides Text-based and Vision-based worlds to localize perception versus reasoning failures.

g.text: After active exploration, we evaluate the process along two axes:
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) After active exploration, we evaluate the process along two axes:

g.text: (i) belief exploitation via spatial downstream tasks that probe
g.title: N15a [Method: belief-exploitation] (cites=2) (i) belief exploitation via spatial downstream tasks that probe route-level and survey-level knowledge (Siegel & White, 1975; Montello, 1998);

g.text: and (ii) exploration efficiency via the number of exploration
steps and the accumulated information gain curve over steps,
capturing how quickly an agent reduces uncertainty rather than
g.title: N15b [Method: exploration-efficiency] (cites=0) and (ii) exploration efficiency via the number of exploration steps and the accumulated information gain curve over steps, capturing how quickly an agent reduces uncertainty rather than merely increasing coverage.

g.text: Finally, we design scripted proxy agents that execute strong
reference trajectories to disentangle exploration from reasoning.
g.title: N16 [Method] (cites=0) Finally, we design scripted proxy agents that execute strong reference trajectories to disentangle exploration from reasoning.

g.text: Our evaluation of state-of-the-art foundation models reveals both
promising capability in the pure text world and striking
limitations in the vision world under THEORY OF SPACE.
g.title: N17 [Result] (cites=0) Our evaluation of state-of-the-art foundation models reveals both promising capability in the pure text world and striking limitations in the vision world under THEORY OF SPACE.

g.text: Active exploration remains a primary bottleneck.
g.title: N18 [Result] (cites=0) Active exploration remains a primary bottleneck.

g.text: Models perform reasonablely well in passive setting, but degrade
when they must actively gather information (e.g., GPT-5.2: 57.1 →
g.title: N19 [Result] (cites=0) Models perform reasonablely well in passive setting, but degrade when they must actively gather information (e.g., GPT-5.2: 57.1 → 46.0; GEMINI-3 PRO: 60.5 → 57.3; Figure. 2).
P19 [Proof] (cites=0) Figure. 2

g.text: We also find a major efficiency gap: rule-based proxy agents reach target
coverage in ∼ 9 steps, whereas foundation models explore redundantly,
requiring ≥ 14 steps without improving belief accuracy.
g.title: N20 [Result] (cites=0) We also find a major efficiency gap: rule-based proxy agents reach target coverage in ∼ 9 steps, whereas foundation models explore redundantly, requiring ≥ 14 steps without improving belief accuracy.

g.text: models can reason but not gather
Thus, even when models can reason about spatial tasks (as reflected in
passive performance), they fail to autonomously structure the
g.title: N21 [Result] (cites=0) Thus, even when models can reason about spatial tasks (as reflected in passive performance), they fail to autonomously structure the information-gathering needed to solve them.

g.text: Beyond downstream task scores, a core contribution of THEORY OF SPACE is
explicit cognitive-map probing, which provides a direct window into the
agent's latent spatial belief as it is constructed and revised.
g.title: N22 [Contribution: cognitive-map-probing] (cites=0) Beyond downstream task scores, a core contribution of THEORY OF SPACE is explicit cognitive-map probing, which provides a direct window into the agent's latent spatial belief as it is constructed and revised.

g.text: prompt model to expose cognitive map
Rather than treating the agent as a black
box whose internal state is only inferred
from final answers, we prompt the model to
expose its evolving cognitive map during…
g.title: N23 [Method] (cites=0) Rather than treating the agent as a black box whose internal state is only inferred from final answers, we prompt the model to expose its evolving cognitive map during exploration, enabling measurement of both belief accuracy and belief uncertainty at each step.

g.text: This probing-based assessment uniquely supports fine-grained
diagnosis of how models represent space: it reveals that while
perception acts as an initial bottleneck, global beliefs also
suffer severely from instability, causing knowledge…
g.title: N24 [Result] (cites=0) This probing-based assessment uniquely supports fine-grained diagnosis of how models represent space: it reveals that while perception acts as an initial bottleneck, global beliefs also suffer severely from instability, causing knowledge to degrade over time.

g.text: This allows us to track belief evolution
over time, attribute failures to specific
whether an agent truly "knows what is…
g.title: N25 [Method] (cites=0) This allows us to track belief evolution over time, attribute failures to specific representational breakdowns, and evaluate whether an agent truly "knows what is uncertain" rather than merely producing plausible outputs.

g.text: Finally, to evaluate the mechanics of dynamic spatial updating, we
g.title: N26 [Method] (cites=0) Finally, to evaluate the mechanics of dynamic spatial updating, we introduce a False Belief paradigm.

g.text: By altering the environment (relocating or reorienting objects)
after the agent's initial exploration, we uncover a phenomenon we
term spatial belief inertia: agents (particularly in vision-based
g.title: N27 [Result] (cites=0) By altering the environment (relocating or reorienting objects) after the agent's initial exploration, we uncover a phenomenon we term spatial belief inertia: agents (particularly in vision-based settings) struggle to overwrite obsolete spatial priors with new sensory evidence.

g.text: Despite directly observing the new configuration, models persist
in their initial, now incorrect coordinates.
g.title: N28 [Result] (cites=0) Despite directly observing the new configuration, models persist in their initial, now incorrect coordinates.

g.text: This reveals a critical failure in spatial memory revision, where
foundational models lack the plasticity to revise their internal
cognitive maps in response to physical changes.
g.title: N29 [Result] (cites=0) This reveals a critical failure in spatial memory revision, where foundational models lack the plasticity to revise their internal cognitive maps in response to physical changes.

g.text: An important direction for future work is to extend
THEORY OF SPACE beyond single-agent settings to
arise around coordination and aligning (or sharing)…
g.title: N30 [Context] (cites=0) An important direction for future work is to extend THEORY OF SPACE beyond single-agent settings to multi-agent exploration, where additional challenges arise around coordination and aligning (or sharing) spatial beliefs across agents.
